subject: Methylated bases in the tile region are not apparent

messages.author: 5f9b59a0042f3023
messages.subject: Methylated bases in the tile region are not apparent
parts:
Hello, 

I would really appreciate some help on this matter. I am trying to understand how methylkit calculates differential methylation between control and treated in a "tile" ? and how it is different from single base resolution analysis ? I am asking because when I view the coordinates falling under differentially methylated region on Integrated Genome Viewer (IGV) using my SAM files, I feel the difference for many regions is not clearly apparent. There is some difference in the region but not every cytosine in that region has more than 25% difference between control and treated. Any explanation on this matter will be very helpful.

Thanks

Aditi

messages.author: ab8277113f65c05e
messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] Methylated bases in the tile region are not apparent
parts:
Hi,
for the CpGs that have coverage in a given tile or region, number of Cs and number of Ts are summed up. You can think of this sth like a weighted average of methylation values, weighted by coverage in this case. Looking at IGV browser for visually inspecting such regions may not yield what you expect. First, there is a summary process per tile as described above second some CpGs may not be included based on coverage and quality threshold when processing the SAM file.


Best,
Altuna

Hello, 

Thanks for your response. I understand weighted average and so from there stems another question. If there is less than 10X coverage in control and more than 10X coverage in that region for infected then are the low coverage regions summarized as zero in control ? Please see the attached image for clarification, this is screenshot of a region called DM by methykit (using 200bp tile and 10X coverage cutoff) but only difference I see there is in the coverage between infected and control. Please let me know how methylkit deals with this problem. Thanks

Aditi
